key_insight: MPFlow learns which Lightning Network channels to open under a fixed budget by directly optimizing max-flow, improving routing capacity through graph reinforcement learning.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical decision tool for liquidity placement in payment networks, helping operators allocate limited capital to channels that most increase throughput.
method: Formulate channel selection as a budgeted k-edge addition problem maximizing s-t max-flow.
Use a message-passing policy network trained with PPO and action masking.
Apply a hub-exclusion curriculum to prevent shortcut learning from simply attaching to top hubs.
evidence_signal: The paper reports strong results on real Lightning Network snapshots across multiple seeds and unseen graphs, and notes production deployment with 4,640 channel-open decisions totaling 267.3 BTC across 30 nodes.
watch_item: Performance depends on graph distribution and training curriculum, so deployment should be validated carefully on new network conditions and changing liquidity patterns.
paper_title: MPFlow: Learning Budgeted Max-Flow Optimization on the Lightning Network with Deep Graph Reinforcement Learning
